author: MiyoMeOhMy
title: Clickbait Mess
content:
So I’ve been playing the game for a while, I don’t even know what to say. It’s NOT as advertised. The mom and kid are privileged and merely have to clean up the restaurant and they’re fine. No worries about the kid eating snow or having a random accident lol. Besides that, the plot is written like a teen wrote it. Our protag is weird and wishy washy and has the attention span of a goldfish.

I could forgive all of that because the merging aspect is not as dumb as other merge games. Cupcake becomes a small cake becomes a large cake and then a larger cake. Makes sense. Unlike other games, the merging makes sense.

I could forgive that the events do not give you enough time to finish them (for free anyway.) And I could forgive that there is only 100 energy and ONLY ever 100 energy allowed to be recharged because you can somewhat manage to play well for a while.

What I CANNOT forgive is that this game is impossible to play the longer you play it. The 100 energy limit is absolutely awful for higher levels— you barely have enough to start any order cuz the orders become impossibly larger. And the game doesn’t throw you much freebies that you can merge to help you reach say, the giant Lvl 10 lobster meal or whatever because they give you the small Lvl 1-5 things. The rewards for most things are hardly worth the effort too for mini games and mini events! I feel like I need at least 200 energy to get anywhere at the game level I’m at: 30+. I’ve even spent money a little to get farther in events and not even that helps— I wish I had a refund cuz I feel dumb for thinking those little packs would get me far into any event. The game basically begs you to pay money at higher levels and I don’t forgive any of this stuff. I’m starting to regret playing it— and I feel like starting over itself isn’t a good idea either. No wins here at all. Smh. I hate how I have like 8 gems, unlocked the bonus reward thing, and I have mostly nothing to show for it.

Btw don’t do the weird Story Mode quests— they are a waste of energy and a waste of time. The rewards suck! And merging to the rocketship or dog or whatever takes so long that the tiny reward won’t be worth it.

Overall, I wish I had my time and money back. I liked the merging and yes there is no ads but that’s it. Ugh.

author: karara107
title: Not like the ads
content:
Most games are not like their ads, which I accept, but I think it’s a special brand of crummy when ads repeatedly say “Don’t you hate it when a game isn’t like the ad? Don’t you wish you had a game that was like all those ads? Well that’s us! We’re just like our ads!”

No, you’re not. 

I don’t generally like merge games, but was willing to give it a try in hopes it did match the ads, and because it highlighted the story as a key feature.

The story makes no sense, to a degree that it feels like they changed their minds halfway through development about what they wanted the story to be, and then didn’t update all the dialogue to match the new direction. Didn’t we start by saying this was her restaurant she was running with her husband, that was then destroyed by rioters (wtf) after people were literally poisoned there? Why does she keep having to explain to people that she owns the restaurant with her husband, and doing things like introducing her daughter to her “best friend?” Haven’t they been living in this town already? 

Seems like the story was originally the classic moving back to your hometown and inheriting a dilapidated building, but for some reason they changed it to sabotage and possible attempted murder.

In any case, it’s not at all like the ads (shocker). I played for a while anyway, but around the time the 8th or 9th concurrent “special event” popped up on the side of the screen, I realized I wasn’t actually having any fun. I was content to just delete it, but in the hour and a half total I’ve spent since then playing other games, I’ve gotten easily a dozen of their disingenuous and/or bizarrely emotionally manipulative ads telling me how this game is the one I’ve been searching for. It’s not.

author: Areadien
title: Fun, but not "that game"
content: This game is fun, but it's not the advertised game as it claims to be. Certain elements are, like being (almost) ad-free (except for optimal things like more energy and such) and the mom is a divorcée. The divorce happens because Quinn finds her husband Colin surrounded by other women at a casino, but she's not unhoused or living in squalor, she doesn't have to give a baby up for adoption--in fact, she doesn't have a baby at all--and you don't use merging to help her rebuild her home. Instead, you have to rebuild her restaurant after people set fire to it, which you find out is related to food poisonings that happened there. In the process, you try to find out who set fire to it and who was behind the poisoning. I did not get that far to find out because, while the game is fun, the lying got to me. That said, if you don't mind that it's not the game it pretends to be, then it's a good game to play.
